pl-l4d39c2-d1e115.summary: Notes that this seems opposed by Paul on unequal marriages: I say, not the Lord, if a brother has an unbelieving wife who consents to live with him, let him not dismiss her.

pl-l4d39c2-d1e124.summary: Quotes Augustine showing the cases differ: the prohibition concerns marriages contracted by believers and unbelievers remaining in different religions; the Apostle concerns those of one unbelief when joined, one of whom believed when the Gospel came.
claims: The prohibition and Paul's counsel concern different cases.

pl-l4d39c2-d1e135.summary: Continues Augustine: two spouses of one unbelief were married, raising no question of the prohibition; the preacher came and one believed, the other consenting to live with the believer; the Lord does not command the believer to dismiss such a spouse, nor does the Apostle command him not to, but counsels it, so that one acting otherwise does not transgress; it is an occasion of gain; what is lawful is not expedient when it hinders others' salvation.
claims: The believer is counseled, not commanded, to remain.

pl-l4d39c2-d1e157.summary: Draws out that there is marriage even among unbelievers, and that the Apostle's counsel does not oppose the Lord's command that a believer not be joined to an unbeliever and, if joined, be separated; so Ezra had the Israelites dismiss foreign wives, contracted against God's prohibition, since, as Ambrose says, a marriage made outside God's decree is not counted, but must be corrected when known.
claims: Marriages contrary to God's prohibition are to be corrected.

pl-l4d39c2-d1e169.summary: Quotes Augustine: when the Gospel was preached to the gentiles, it found them married; if one believed and the other consented to live together, the Lord neither forbade nor commanded the believer to leave: not forbade, since justice permits leaving a fornicator, and the unbeliever's fornication is in the heart; not commanded, since they were not married against the Lord's command. It was lawful by justice to leave, but not to be done, out of free benevolence.
claims: Leaving is just but not advisable.

pl-l4d39c2-d1e184.summary: Concludes that there is marriage among unbelievers and that the Apostle concerns those joined in unbelief, one later converted, with whom the unbeliever consents to live; the Apostle counsels the believer not to dismiss such a spouse, since perhaps the unbeliever will be saved through the believer.
claims: The believer should stay so the unbeliever may be saved.

pl-l4d39c2.summary: Paul's counsel that a believer not dismiss an unbelieving spouse who consents to live together seems opposed, but Augustine shows it concerns spouses married as unbelievers, one of whom later believed, not marriages contracted across religions. The Lord neither commands nor forbids the believer to leave such a spouse; the Apostle counsels staying, as an occasion of winning the other. So there is marriage among unbelievers, and Paul's counsel does not contradict the prohibition of mixed marriage, as Ezra's dismissal of foreign wives shows; the believer may justly leave, the unbeliever's fornication being in the heart, but charity counsels against it.
claims: Paul's counsel concerns spouses married as unbelievers, one later converting.
There is true marriage among unbelievers.
The believer may leave but is counseled to stay for the other's salvation.
